14004: Let, I pray Thee be ended the evil of the wicked, And establish Thou the righteous, And a trier of hearts and reins is the righteous God.
14009: Lo, he travaileth with iniquity, And he hath conceived perverseness, And hath brought forth falsehood.
14010: A pit he hath prepared, and he diggeth it, And he falleth into a ditch he maketh.
14013: To the Overseer, ‘On the Gittith.’ A Psalm of David. Jehovah, our Lord, How honourable Thy name in all the earth! Who settest thine honour on the heavens.
14014: From the mouths of infants and sucklings Thou hast founded strength, Because of Thine adversaries, To still an enemy and a self-avenger.
14017: And causest him to lack a little of Godhead, And with honour and majesty compassest him.
14022: To the Overseer, ‘On the Death of Labben.’—A Psalm of David. I confess, O Jehovah, with all my heart, I recount all Thy wonders,
14026: Thou hast rebuked nations, Thou hast destroyed the wicked, Their name Thou hast blotted out to the age and for ever.
14027: O thou Enemy, Finished have been destructions for ever, As to cities thou hast plucked up, Perished hath their memorial with them.
14041: Appoint, O Jehovah, a director to them, Let nations know they are men! Selah.
14043: Through the pride of the wicked, Is the poor inflamed, They are caught in devices that they devised.
14044: Because the wicked hath boasted Of the desire of his soul, And a dishonest gainer he hath blessed, He hath despised Jehovah.
14046: Pain do his ways at all times, On high are Thy judgments before him, All his adversaries—he puffeth at them.
14048: Of oaths his mouth is full, And deceits, and fraud: Under his tongue is perverseness and iniquity,
14052: He said in his heart, ‘God hath forgotten, He hath hid His face, He hath never seen.’
14055: Thou hast seen, For Thou perverseness and anger beholdest; By giving into Thy hand, On Thee doth the afflicted leave it, Of the fatherless Thou hast been an helper.
14061: For lo, the wicked tread a bow, They have prepared their arrow on the string, To shoot in darkness at the upright in heart.
14068: Vanity they speak each with his neighbour, Lip of flattery! With heart and heart they speak.
14074: Around the wicked walk continually, According as vileness is exalted by sons of men!
14077: Look attentively; Answer me, O Jehovah, my God, Enlighten mine eyes, lest I sleep in death,
14078: Lest mine enemy say, ‘I overcame him,’ Mine adversaries joy when I am moved.
14080: I do sing to Jehovah, For He hath conferred benefits upon me!
14089: He who is walking uprightly, And working righteousness, And speaking truth in his heart.
14090: He hath not slandered by his tongue, He hath not done to his friend evil; And reproach he hath not lifted up Against his neighbour.
14097: Jehovah is the portion of my share, and of my cup, Thou—Thou dost uphold my lot.
14103: Thou causest me to know the path of life; Fulness of joys is with Thy presence, Pleasant things by Thy right hand for ever!
14110: Separate wonderfully Thy kindness, O Saviour of the confiding, By Thy right hand, from withstanders.
14117: From men, Thy hand, O Jehovah, From men of the world, their portion is in life, And with Thy hidden things Thou fillest their belly, They are satisfied with sons; And have left their abundance to their sucklings.
14132: And He sendeth His arrows and scattereth them, And much lightning, and crusheth them.
14143: With the kind Thou showest Thyself kind, With a perfect man showest Thyself perfect.
14146: For Thou—Thou lightest my lamp, Jehovah my God enlighteneth my darkness.
14175: The law of Jehovah is perfect, refreshing the soul, The testimonies of Jehovah are stedfast, Making wise the simple,
14176: The precepts of Jehovah are upright, Rejoicing the heart, The command of Jehovah is pure, enlightening the eyes,
14178: They are more desirable than gold, Yea, than much fine gold; and sweeter than honey, Even liquid honey of the comb.
14180: Errors! who doth understand? From hidden ones declare me innocent,
14181: Also—from presumptuous ones keep back Thy servant, Let them not rule over me, Then am I perfect, And declared innocent of much transgression,
14185: He doth remember all thy presents, And thy burnt-offering doth reduce to ashes. Selah.
14187: We sing of thy salvation, And in the name of our God set up a banner. Jehovah doth fulfil all thy requests.
14192: To the Overseer.—A Psalm of David. Jehovah, in Thy strength is the king joyful, In Thy salvation how greatly he rejoiceth.
14199: Thy hand cometh to all Thine enemies, Thy right hand doth find Thy haters.
14203: For Thou makest them a butt, When Thy strings Thou preparest against their faces.
14216: Many bulls have surrounded me, Mighty ones of Bashan have compassed me,
14218: As waters I have been poured out, And separated themselves have all my bones, My heart hath been like wax, It is melted in the midst of my bowels.
14219: Dried up as an earthen vessel is my power, And my tongue is cleaving to my jaws.
14220: And to the dust of death thou appointest me, For surrounded me have dogs, A company of evil doers have compassed me, Piercing my hands and my feet.
14229: Of Thee my praise is in the great assembly. My vows I complete before His fearers.
14237: In pastures of tender grass He causeth me to lie down, By quiet waters He doth lead me.
14238: My soul He refresheth, He leadeth me in paths of righteousness, For His name’s sake,
14240: Thou arrangest before me a table, Over-against my adversaries, Thou hast anointed with oil my head, My cup is full!
14254: Also let none waiting on Thee be ashamed, Let the treacherous dealers without cause be ashamed.
14257: Remember Thy mercies, O Jehovah, And Thy kindnesses, for from the age are they.
14267: Turn Thou unto me, and favour me, For lonely and afflicted am I.
14277: I have not sat with vain men, And with dissemblers I enter not.
14283: In whose hand is a wicked device, And their right hand is full of bribes.
14285: My foot hath stood in uprightness, In assemblies I bless Jehovah!
14291: And now, lifted up is my head, Above my enemies—my surrounders, And I sacrifice in His tent sacrifices of shouting, I sing, yea, I sing praise to Jehovah.
14300: By David. Unto Thee, O Jehovah, I call, My rock, be not silent to me! Lest Thou be silent to me, And I have been compared With those going down to the pit.
14304: For they attend not to the doing of Jehovah, And unto the work of His hands. He throweth them down, And doth not build them up.
14311: The voice of Jehovah is on the waters, The God of glory hath thundered, Jehovah is on many waters.
14313: The voice of Jehovah is shivering cedars, Yea, Jehovah shivers the cedars of Lebanon.
14314: And He causeth them to skip as a calf, Lebanon and Sirion as a son of Reems,
14316: The voice of Jehovah paineth a wilderness, Jehovah paineth the wilderness of Kadesh.
14324: For—a moment is in His anger, Life is in His good-will, At even remaineth weeping, and at morn singing.
14334: For my rock and my bulwark art Thou, For Thy name’s sake lead me and tend me.
14338: I rejoice, and am glad in Thy kindness, In that Thou hast seen mine affliction, Thou hast known in adversities my soul.
14351: Thou hast wrought for those trusting in Thee, Before sons of men. Thou hidest them in the secret place of Thy presence, From artifices of man, Thou concealest them in a tabernacle, From the strife of tongues.
14352: Blessed is Jehovah, For He hath made marvellous His kindness To me in a city of bulwarks.
14357: O the happiness of a man, To whom Jehovah imputeth not iniquity, And in whose spirit there is no deceit.
14359: When by day and by night Thy hand is heavy upon me, My moisture hath been changed Into the droughts of summer. Selah.
14364: Be ye not as a horse—as a mule, Without understanding, With bridle and bit, its ornaments, to curb, Not to come near unto thee.
14369: Sing ye to Him a new song, Play skilfully with shouting.
14392: I sought Jehovah, and He answered me, And from all my fears did deliver me.
14395: A messenger of Jehovah is encamping, Round about those who fear Him, And He armeth them.
14396: Taste ye and see that Jehovah is good, O the happiness of the man who trusteth in Him.
14411: By David. Strive, Jehovah, with my strivers, fight with my fighters,
14416: Their way is darkness and slipperiness, And a messenger of Jehovah their pursuer.
14417: For without cause they hid for me their netpit, Without cause they digged for my soul.
14420: All my bones say, ‘Jehovah, who is like Thee, Delivering the poor from the stronger than he, And the poor and needy from his plunderer.’
14422: They pay me evil for good, bereaving my soul,
14425: And—in my halting they have rejoiced, And have been gathered together, Gathered against me were the smiters, And I have not known, They have rent, and they have not ceased;
14426: With profane ones, mockers in feasts, Gnashing against me their teeth.
14427: Lord, how long dost thou behold? Keep back my soul from their desolations, From young lions my only one.
14429: Mine enemies rejoice not over me with falsehood, Those hating me without cause wink the eye.
14430: For they speak not peace, And against the quiet of the land, Deceitful words they devise,
14437: They sing and rejoice, who are desiring my righteousness, And they say continually, ‘Jehovah is magnified, Who is desiring the peace of His servant.’
14439: To the Overseer.—By a servant of Jehovah, by David. The transgression of the wicked Is affirming within my heart, ‘Fear of God is not before his eyes,
14441: The words of his mouth are iniquity and deceit, He ceased to act prudently—to do good.
14442: Iniquity he deviseth on his bed, He stationeth himself on a way not good, Evil he doth not refuse.’
14450: There have workers of iniquity fallen, They have been overthrown, And have not been able to arise!
14451: By David. Do not fret because of evil doers, Be not envious against doers of iniquity,
14454: And delight thyself on Jehovah, And He giveth to thee the petitions of thy heart.
14467: For the arms of the wicked are shivered, And Jehovah is sustaining the righteous.
14470: But the wicked perish, and the enemies of Jehovah, As the preciousness of lambs, Have been consumed, In smoke they have been consumed.
14471: The wicked is borrowing and repayeth not, And the righteous is gracious and giving.
14476: All the day he is gracious and lending, And his seed is for a blessing.
14488: And transgressors were destroyed together, The latter end of the wicked was cut off.
14493: Soundness is not in my flesh, Because of Thine indignation, Peace is not in my bones because of my sin.
14495: Stunk—become corrupt have my wounds, Because of my folly.
14498: I have been feeble and smitten—unto excess, I have roared from disquietude of heart.
14500: My heart is panting, my power hath forsaken me, And the light of mine eyes, Even they are not with me.
14501: My lovers and my friends over-against my plague stand. And my neighbours afar off have stood.
14502: And those seeking my soul lay a snare, And those seeking my evil Have spoken mischievous things, And they do deceits meditate all the day.
14504: Yea, I am as a man who heareth not, And in his mouth are no reproofs.
14506: When I said, ‘Lest they rejoice over me, In the slipping of my foot against me they magnified themselves.
14507: For I am ready to halt, And my pain is before me continually.
14508: For mine iniquity I declare, I am sorry for my sin.
14510: And those paying evil for good accuse me, Because of my pursuing good.
14514: I was dumb with silence, I kept silent from good, and my pain is excited.
14516: Cause me to know, O Jehovah, mine end, And the measure of my days—what it is,’ I know how frail I am.
14517: Lo, handbreadths Thou hast made my days, And mine age is as nothing before Thee, Only, all vanity is every man set up. Selah.
14518: Only, in an image doth each walk habitually, Only, in vain, they are disquieted, He heapeth up and knoweth not who gathereth them.
14523: With reproofs against iniquity, Thou hast corrected man, And dost waste as a moth his desirableness, Only, vanity is every man. Selah.
14527: And He doth cause me to come up From a pit of desolation—from mire of mud, And He raiseth up on a rock my feet, He is establishing my steps.
14536: Thou, O Jehovah, restrainest not Thy mercies from me, Thy kindness and Thy truth do continually keep me.
14537: For compassed me have evils innumerable, Overtaken me have mine iniquities, And I have not been able to see; They have been more than the hairs of my head, And my heart hath forsaken me.
14549: All hating me whisper together against me, Against me they devise evil to me:
14550: A thing of Belial is poured out on him, And because he lay down he riseth not again.
14551: Even mine ally, in whom I trusted, One eating my bread, made great the heel against me,
14553: By this I have known, That Thou hast delighted in me, Because my enemy shouteth not over me.
14556: To the Overseer.—An Instruction. By sons of Korah. As a hart doth pant for streams of water, So my soul panteth toward Thee, O God.
14557: My soul thirsted for God, for the living God, When do I enter and see the face of God?
14559: These I remember, and pour out my soul in me, For I pass over into the booth, I go softly with them unto the house of God, With the voice of singing and confession, The multitude keeping feast!
14560: What! bowest thou thyself, O my soul? Yea, art thou troubled within me? Wait for God, for still I confess Him: The salvation of my countenance—My God!
14561: In me doth my soul bow itself, Therefore I remember Thee from the land of Jordan, And of the Hermons, from the hill Mizar.
14562: Deep unto deep is calling At the noise of Thy water-spouts, All Thy breakers and Thy billows passed over me.
14573: Thou, with Thy hand, nations hast dispossessed. And Thou dost plant them. Thou afflictest peoples, and sendest them away.
14575: Thou art He, my king, O God, Command the deliverances of Jacob.
14584: Thou makest us a reproach to our neighbours, A scorn and a reproach to our surrounders.
14587: Because of the voice of a reproacher and reviler, Because of an enemy and a self-avenger.
14595: Why Thy face hidest Thou? Thou forgettest our afflictions and our oppression,
14598: To the Overseer.—‘On the Lilies.’—By sons of Korah.—An Instruction.—A song of loves. My heart hath indited a good thing, I am telling my works to a king, My tongue is the pen of a speedy writer.
14601: As to Thy majesty—prosper!—ride! Because of truth, and meekness—righteousness, And Thy right hand showeth Thee fearful things.
14604: Thou hast loved righteousness and hatest wickedness, Therefore God, thy God, hath anointed thee, Oil of joy above thy companions.
14620: Troubled have been nations, Moved have been kingdoms, He hath given forth with His voice, earth melteth.
14622: Come ye, see the works of Jehovah, Who hath done astonishing things in the earth,
14623: Causing wars to cease, Unto the end of the earth, the bow he shivereth, And the spear He hath cut asunder, Chariots he doth burn with fire.
14626: To the Overseer.—By sons of Korah. A Psalm. All ye peoples, clap the hand, Shout to God with a voice of singing,
14639: They have seen—so they have marvelled, They have been troubled, they were hastened away.
14640: Trembling hath seized them there, Pain, as of a travailing woman.
14641: By an east wind Thou shiverest ships of Tarshish.
14647: Set your heart to her bulwark, Consider her high places, So that ye recount to a later generation,
14651: My mouth speaketh wise things, And the meditations of my heart are things of understanding.
14653: Why do I fear in days of evil? The iniquity of my supplanters doth compass me.
14658: For he seeth wise men die, Together the foolish and brutish perish, And have left to others their wealth.
14671: Our God cometh, and is not silent, Fire before Him doth devour, And round about him it hath been very tempestuous.
14683: And call Me in a day of adversity, I deliver thee, and thou honourest Me.
14686: If thou hast seen a thief, Then thou art pleased with him, And with adulterers is thy portion.
14688: Thou sittest, against thy brother thou speakest, Against a son of thy mother givest slander.
14691: He who is sacrificing praise honoureth Me, As to him who maketh a way, I cause him to look on the salvation of God!
14698: Thou cleansest me with hyssop and I am clean, Washest me, and than snow I am whiter.
14707: For Thou desirest not sacrifice, or I give it, Burnt-offering Thou acceptest not.
14711: To the Overseer.—An instruction, by David, in the coming in of Doeg the Edomite, and he declareth to Saul, and saith to him, ‘David came in unto the house of Ahimelech.’ What, boasteth thou in evil, O mighty one? The kindness of God is all the day.
14714: Thou hast loved all devouring words, O thou deceitful tongue.
14715: Also—God doth break thee down for ever, Taketh thee, and pulleth thee out of the tent, And He hath uprooted thee Out of the land of the living. Selah.
14726: To the Overseer with stringed instruments.—An instruction, by David, in the coming in of the Ziphim, and they say to Saul, ‘Is not David hiding himself with us?’ O God, by Thy name save me, and by Thy might judge me.
14737: Fear and trembling come in to me, And horror doth cover me.
14752: He hath sent forth his hands against his well-wishers, He hath polluted his covenant.
14753: Sweeter than honey hath been his mouth, And his heart is war! Softer have been his words than oil, And they are drawn swords.
14760: All the day they wrest my words, Concerning me all their thoughts are for evil,
14769: To the Overseer.—‘Destroy not.’—A secret treasure of David, in his fleeing from the face of Saul into a cave. Favour me, O God, favour me, For in Thee is my soul trusting, And in the shadow of Thy wings I trust, Until the calamities pass over.
14770: I call to God Most High, To God who is perfecting for me.
14781: Even in heart ye work iniquities, In the land the violence of your hands ye ponder.
14783: Their poison is as poison of a serpent, As a deaf asp shutting its ear,
14784: Which hearkeneth not to the voice of whisperers, A charmer of charms most skilful.
14787: As a snail that melteth he goeth on, As an untimely birth of a woman, They have not seen the sun.
14788: Before your pots discern the bramble, As well the raw as the heated He whirleth away.
14797: Lo, they belch out with their mouths, Swords are in their lips, for ‘Who heareth?’
14809: Thou hast caused the land to tremble, Thou hast broken it, Heal its breaches, for it hath moved.
14821: From the end of the land unto Thee I call, In the feebleness of my heart, Into a rock higher than I Thou dost lead me.
14825: Days to the days of the king Thou addest, His years as generation and generation.
14830: Till when do ye devise mischief against a man? Ye are destroyed all of you, As a wall inclined, a hedge that is cast down.
14831: Only—from his excellency They have consulted to drive away, They enjoy a lie, with their mouth they bless, And with their heart revile. Selah.
14840: A Psalm of David, in his being in the wilderness of Judah. O God, Thou art my God, earnestly do I seek Thee, Thirsted for Thee hath my soul, Longed for Thee hath my flesh, In a land dry and weary, without waters.
14850: And the king doth rejoice in God, Boast himself doth every one swearing by Him, But stopped is the mouth of those speaking lies!
14856: They search out perverse things, ‘We perfected a searching search,’ And the inward part of man, and the heart are deep.
14857: And God doth shoot them with an arrow, Sudden have been their wounds,
14858: And they cause him to stumble, Against them is their own tongue, Every looker on them fleeth away.
14864: O the happiness of him whom Thou choosest, And drawest near, he inhabiteth Thy courts, We are satisfied with the goodness of Thy house, Thy holy temple.
14868: And the inhabitants of the uttermost parts From Thy signs are afraid, The outgoings of morning and evening Thou causest to sing.
14869: Thou hast inspected the earth, and waterest it, Thou makest it very rich, the rivulet of God is full of water, Thou preparest their corn, When thus Thou dost prepare it,
14870: Its ridges have been filled, Deepened hath been its furrow, With showers Thou dost soften it, Its springing up Thou blessest.
14871: Thou hast crowned the year of Thy goodness, And Thy paths drop fatness.
14883: For Thou hast tried us, O God, Thou hast refined us as the refining of silver.
14897: Rejoice and sing do nations, For Thou judgest peoples uprightly, And peoples on earth comfortest. Selah.
14902: As the driving away of smoke Thou drivest away, As the melting of wax before fire, The wicked perish at the presence of God.
14904: Sing ye to God—praise His name, Raise up a highway for Him who is riding in deserts, In Jah is His name, and exult before Him.
14909: A shower of free-will gifts thou shakest out, O God. Thine inheritance, when it hath been weary, Thou hast established it.
14911: The Lord doth give the saying, The female proclaimers are a numerous host.
14913: Though ye do lie between two boundaries, Wings of a dove covered with silver, And her pinions with yellow gold.
14921: Only—God doth smite The head of His enemies, The hairy crown of a habitual walker in his guilt.
14923: So that thou dashest thy foot in blood, In the blood of enemies—the tongue of Thy dogs.’
14925: Singers have been before, Behind are players on instruments, In the midst virgins playing with timbrels.
14930: Rebuke a beast of the reeds, a company of bulls, With calves of the peoples, Each humbling himself with pieces of silver, Scatter Thou peoples delighting in conflicts.
14937: I have sunk in deep mire, And there is no standing, I have come into the depths of the waters, And a flood hath overflown me.
14943: A stranger I have been to my brother, And a foreigner to sons of my mother.
14944: For zeal for Thy house hath consumed me, And the reproaches of Thy reproachers Have fallen upon me.
14949: Deliver me from the mire, and let me not sink, Let me be delivered from those hating me, And from deep places of waters.
14950: Let not a flood of waters overflow me, Nor let the deep swallow me up, Nor let the pit shut her mouth upon me.
14955: Reproach hath broken my heart, and I am sick, And I look for a bemoaner, and there is none, And for comforters, and I have found none.
14960: Their tower is desolated, In their tents there is no dweller.
14966: And it is better to Jehovah than an ox, A bullock—horned—hoofed.
14989: They are ashamed, they are consumed, Who are opposing my soul, They are covered with reproach and blushing, Who are seeking my evil,
14996: Because Thou hast showed me many and sad distresses, Thou turnest back—Thou revivest me, And from the depths of the earth, Thou turnest back—Thou bringest me up.
14997: Thou dost increase my greatness, And Thou surroundest—Thou comfortest me,
15004: He judgeth the poor of the people, Giveth deliverance to the sons of the needy, And bruiseth the oppressor.
15006: He cometh down as rain on mown grass, As showers—sprinkling the earth.
15008: And he ruleth from sea unto sea, And from the river unto the ends of earth.
15020: The prayers of David son of Jesse have been ended.
15025: In the misery of mortals they are not, And with common men they are not plagued.
15026: Therefore hath pride encircled them, Violence covereth them as a dress.
15027: Their eye hath come out from fat. The imaginations of the heart transgressed;
15032: Lo, these are the wicked and easy ones of the age, They have increased strength.
15038: Only, in slippery places Thou dost set them, Thou hast caused them to fall to desolations.
15040: As a dream from awakening, O Lord, In awaking, their image Thou despisest.
15041: For my heart doth show itself violent, And my reins prick themselves,
15048: And I—nearness of God to me is good, I have placed in the Lord Jehovah my refuge, To recount all Thy works!
15049: An Instruction of Asaph. Why, O God, hast Thou cast off for ever? Thine anger smoketh against the flock of Thy pasture.
15051: Lift up Thy steps to the perpetual desolations, Everything the enemy did wickedly in the sanctuary.
15054: And now, its carvings together With axe and hatchet they break down,
15064: Thine is the day, also Thine is the night, Thou hast prepared a light giver—the sun.
15074: Melted is the earth and all its inhabitants, I—I have pondered its pillars. Selah.
15079: For a cup is in the hand of Jehovah, And the wine hath foamed, It is full of mixture, and He poureth out of it, Only its dregs wring out, and drink, Do all the wicked of the earth,
15089: From heaven Thou hast sounded judgment, Earth hath feared, and hath been still,
15091: For the fierceness of man praiseth Thee, The remnant of fierceness Thou girdest on.
15099: I remember my music in the night, With my heart I meditate, and my spirit doth search diligently:
15111: The voice of Thy thunder is in the spheres, Lightnings have lightened the world, The earth hath trembled, yea, it shaketh.
15112: In the sea is Thy way, And Thy paths are in many waters, And Thy tracks have not been known.
15121: And they are not like their fathers, A generation apostate and rebellious, A generation! it hath not prepared its heart, Nor stedfast with God is its spirit.
15151: And He—the Merciful One, Pardoneth iniquity, and destroyeth not, And hath often turned back His anger, And waketh not up all His fury.
15154: Yea, they turn back, and try God, And the Holy One of Israel have limited.
15162: He sendeth on them the fury of His anger, Wrath, and indignation, and distress—A discharge of evil messengers.
15163: He pondereth a path for His anger, He kept not back their soul from death, Yea, their life to the pestilence He delivered up.
15165: And causeth His people to journey as a flock, And guideth them as a drove in a wilderness,
15169: And they tempt and provoke God Most High, And His testimonies have not kept.
15178: And the Lord waketh as a sleeper, As a mighty one crying aloud from wine.
15185: And he ruleth them according to the integrity of his heart, And by the skilfulness of his hands leadeth them!
15189: We have been a reproach to our neighbours, A scorn and a derision to our surrounders.
15193: Remember not for us the iniquities of forefathers, Haste, let Thy mercies go before us, For we have been very weak.
15203: Thou hast caused them to eat bread of tears, And causest them to drink With tears a third time.
15206: A vine out of Egypt Thou dost bring, Thou dost cast out nations, and plantest it.
15210: Why hast Thou broken down its hedges, And all passing by the way have plucked it?
15211: A boar out of the forest doth waste it, And a wild beast of the fields consumeth it.
15213: And the root that Thy right hand planted, And the branch Thou madest strong for Thee,
15228: But, My people hearkened not to My voice, And Israel hath not consented to Me.
15244: Against Thy people they take crafty counsel, And consult against Thy hidden ones.
15247: Tents of Edom, and Ishmaelites, Moab, and the Hagarenes,
15248: Gebal, and Ammon, and Amalek, Philistia with inhabitants of Tyre,
15251: They were destroyed at Endor, They were dung for the ground!
15256: So dost Thou pursue them with Thy whirlwind, And with Thy hurricane troublest them.
15262: (Even a sparrow hath found a house, And a swallow a nest for herself, Where she hath placed her brood,) Thine altars, O Jehovah of Hosts, My king and my God.
15270: For a sun and a shield is Jehovah God, Grace and honour doth Jehovah give. He withholdeth not good To those walking in uprightness.
15284: Righteousness before Him goeth, And maketh His footsteps for a way!
15289: For Thou, Lord, art good and forgiving. And abundant in kindness to all calling Thee.
15307: Jehovah doth recount in the describing of the peoples, ‘This one was born there.’ Selah.
15309: A Song, a Psalm, by sons of Korah, to the Overseer, ‘Concerning the Sickness of Afflictions.’—An instruction, by Heman the Ezrahite. O Jehovah, God of my salvation, Daily I have cried, nightly before Thee,
15320: Are Thy wonders known in the darkness? And Thy righteousness in the land of forgetfulness?
15322: Why, O Jehovah, castest Thou off my soul? Thou hidest Thy face from me.

15554: Who is satisfying with good thy desire, Renew itself as an eagle doth thy youth.

15575: Making His messengers—the winds, His ministers—the flaming fire.

15591: Thou settest darkness, and it is night, In it doth every beast of the forest creep.
